title: Dashboard
subtitle: Monitor performance, review leaks, and track your technical evolution tournament by tournament.

kpis.roiTooltip: Cumulative return on investment. Positive ROI means you're profiting above the average buy-in. Reference: consistent regular players sit between +20% and +80% in MTTs.
kpis.itmTooltip: Percentage of tournaments where you finished in the money. Field average is ~18%. Above 22% suggests solid or conservative play; below may indicate early bust-outs.
kpis.standardTooltip: Percentage of decisions aligned with the GTO solver (correct + mixed) over the last 90 days. Calculated by comparing your plays against static ranges and solver data. Only decisions with available GTO coverage are counted.
kpis.eventsTooltip: Total volume of analyzed tournaments. Samples smaller than 30 tournaments may have financial results skewed by variance. Decision analysis is reliable from ~500 hands.

aiConfidence.title: AI Confidence
aiConfidence.tooltip: Indicates the reliability of analyses based on data volume. The more tournaments imported, the more accurate the leak recommendations and study plan.

leaks.sourceHeuristicTooltip: Not enough GTO coverage. Leaks computed by the engine's heuristic analysis, may be less precise.

ghost.tooltip: Summary of your drill activity in the last 30 days. Overdue drills (red) indicate spots that need review, skipping them increases the chance of repeating the same mistake in live play.
ghost.title: Ghost Table

bankroll.tooltip: Cumulative financial result curve tournament by tournament. Shows real variance and long-term trend, not just isolated results. Useful for deciding stake adjustments.
bankroll.title: Bankroll evolution

table.title: Recent tournaments

table.gtoCoverageTooltip: Percentage of this tournament's decisions with GTO analysis available. The rest use heuristic classification.
table.qualityTooltip: Session quality: % of decisions on standard (no mistake), by the GTO/heuristic verdict.
table.gtoSplitTooltip: GTO coverage. Preflop uses the GTO Wizard ranges (near-instant). Postflop is solved on demand on the server, coverage grows as you review your hands.

decisions.title: Decision Quality
decisions.tooltip: Distribution of all your decisions by quality. Standard = within expected range (score ≤ 0.08). Marginal = acceptable but suboptimal. Mistakes reduce your long-term ROI.

streets.title: Performance by Street
streets.tooltip: Standard decision rate (score ≤ 0.08) per street. Streets in orange or red indicate where your leaks are concentrated.

positions.title: Performance by Position
positions.tooltip: Standard decision rate by table position. BTN and CO usually have positional advantage. Defensive BB and SB are where most players lose the most equity.

gtoPosition.title: GTO Alignment by Position
gtoPosition.tooltip: GTO alignment breakdown by position, identifies which seat has the most solver divergence over the last 90 days.

gtoNotice.processing_plural: {{n}} spots being processed by the GTO solver, this card will update when analysis completes.

gtoNotice.bannerDesc_plural: {{n}} spots are still being validated by the solver. Your stats will be recomputed automatically as they finish.

form.title: Recent Form
form.tooltip: Average decision quality in recent tournaments. Green = standard session, yellow = marginal, orange/red = session with significant errors.

icm.title: ICM Pressure
icm.tooltip: ICM (Independent Chip Model) measures the monetary value of chips in MTTs. Under high pressure (bubble, FT), mistakes cost much more than the nominal chip value.

pressure.title: Pressure Collapse
pressure.tooltip: Compares your decision quality across ICM pressure levels. A solid player maintains consistent scores regardless of pressure. A delta above 8pts indicates collapse.
pressure.collapseSummary: Score +{{delta}}pts worse under high ICM pressure, focus on bubble and FT spots.
pressure.stableSummary: Stable performance: only {{delta}}pts variation between high pressure and no pressure.

drift.alertDesc: {{n}} recent sessions with technical quality below your baseline, possible tilt or fatigue.

pendingGto.notice: {{n}} GTO spot being analyzed by the solver. Your stats recompute on their own as it validates, {{eta}}.
pendingGto.notice_plural: {{n}} GTO spots being analyzed by the solver. Your stats recompute on their own as it validates, {{eta}}.

gtoQuality.title: GTO Alignment
gtoQuality.tooltip: Distribution of decision quality evaluated by the GTO solver over the last 90 days. Only decisions with available GTO data are counted.

leakFinder.title: Leak Finder
leakFinder.tooltip: Your leaks prioritized by EV LOST (big blinds left on the table), not by error count. The top is where the most EV escapes, start there.
leakFinder.headline_label: left on the table across {{n}} leaked spots
leakFinder.coaching: Attack top-down: fixing leak #1 is worth more than several small ones. Each row is a recurring spot, review it in the Replayer and train it on the Ghost Table.

resultsVsGto.title: Results × GTO
resultsVsGto.tooltip: Decisions that were CLEAR GTO mistakes but the hand was won, the result masks the process error. Winning doesn't validate the play.
resultsVsGto.headline_label: clear GTO mistakes in hands you won
resultsVsGto.stat_won_were_critical: of decisions in won hands were clear mistakes
resultsVsGto.stat_critical_hidden: of your clear mistakes were hidden behind wins
resultsVsGto.coaching: The result masks the process: winning doesn't mean you played it right. Review these spots even when you win.

gtoAlignment.title: GTO Alignment by Street
gtoAlignment.tooltip: GTO alignment breakdown by preflop, flop, turn, and river, identifies which phase of the game has the most solver divergence.

level.tooltip: Your current level based on your average Standard% across recent tournaments. Each level requires a higher threshold of correct decisions, advancing means your mistakes have consistently decreased.
level.title: My Level

tip.solverSeats: Solver, in your seats and stacks

playerStats.tendenciaDirecional: Directional trend vs the MTT benchmark
playerStats.hudResumo: Your playing profile in three rows: preflop initiative (VPIP, PFR, RFI, 3-Bet), preflop situations (Fold to 3-Bet, Steal, Open Limp, BB Defense) and postflop (C-Bet, Fold vs Bet, WTSD, W$SD).

amostra.baixaTooltip: {{n}} hands, wide confidence interval (over ±10pp on VPIP/PFR). With a small sample the numbers are DIRECTIONAL: they show the trend (more tight/loose/passive), not exact values, and a few points either way do not change the read. Aim for 200+ hands for a reliable read; 1000+ for benchmarking.
amostra.mediaTooltip: {{n}} hands, typical CI of ±5pp. Trends are reliable but absolute values still move. Reach 1000+ hands for solid benchmarking.
amostra.robustaTooltip: {{n}} hands, CI under ±3pp. Statistically reliable numbers for comparison against benchmarks.

playerStats.cbetSplitNone: IP / OOP show up once there are heads-up flops.
playerStats.cbetSplitNote: Heads-up pots on the flop only; with two or more opponents it counts in neither. The reference is what the solver would do in each of your spots (P20–P80 of its bet frequency).

dna.title: Strategic Profile
dna.tooltip: Strategic signature based on your real decision patterns. Each axis represents a dimension of your playing style.
dna.noData: Import tournaments to calculate your strategic profile.

archetypeDesc.TAG: Selective and aggressive when entering, winning profile in regular MTTs.
archetypeDesc.LAG: Plays many pots and applies pressure, effective, but requires range calibration.
archetypeDesc.Nit: Folds too much: loses passive equity and gets exploited by regulars.
archetypeDesc.Calling Station: Calls too much: makes it easy for opponents to extract EV.
archetypeDesc.Balanced: Well-rounded profile: good range control across multiple positions.

leakCausalMap.tooltip: Visualizes which leaks co-occur in the same tournaments (across different hands). Thicker lines indicate stronger correlation, when two leaks appear together in the same tournament, they usually share a common root cause.
leakCausalMap.title: Leak Causal Map

cognitiveFailure.tooltip: Detects emotional patterns that affect sequential decision quality, for example, becoming overly aggressive right after folding several hands in a row. Identifying the trigger is the first step to correcting it.
cognitiveFailure.title: Cognitive Patterns

descriptions.revenge_aggression: Aggressive mistakes shortly after a sequence of correct folds
descriptions.fear_folding: Incorrect folds after consecutive aggressive mistakes (blowup hands)
descriptions.sunk_cost: Bad calls across multiple streets of the same hand (chasing the pot)
descriptions.entitlement_tilt: Cascading mistakes after a long streak of correct decisions
descriptions.compensation_call: Incorrect calls in the hands following a correct fold of a strong hand
descriptions.icm_blindness: Risking your stack on thin final-table spots where ICM calls for tightening (survival has value)

strategicTwin.title: Strategic Patterns
strategicTwin.tooltip: Identifies spots (street + action + ICM pressure combinations) where your error rate exceeds your personal average by at least 10%. Reveals costly habits invisible when looking at individual decisions.

strategicTwin.noPatterns: No costly spots detected. Keep playing to refine your analysis.

primeiroAcesso.titulo: Three steps to your first diagnosis
primeiroAcesso.subtitulo: GrindLab reads the files your poker site already saves. Nothing is typed by hand.

p1.ligarPrimeiro: On {{site}}, turn on hand history saving in the settings before you play. Without it the file does not exist.
p1.pasta: The folder is usually this one:
p1.semCaminho: On {{site}}, look for the hand history export option inside the client. If you cannot find it, contact support and we will help.

p2.desc: You can drop several at once. Parsing runs in the background and you can keep browsing.

p3.agora: From the first tournament: your mistakes hand by hand, what GTO would do and what it cost.
p3.depois: With more tournaments: ranked leaks, the study plan and your bankroll curve.
p3.honestidade: One thing takes patience: proving you actually improved needs sample. The product only claims it when the difference survives chance, and says "not enough to tell yet" until it does. That is on purpose.

demo.explicacao: Real data from one player, anonymised. This is not your account.
demo.indisponivel: The demo is unavailable right now.

tour.p1desc: The platform does not hand you a panel and let you guess the next move: it names the leak to attack first, and why. Everything below is evidence for that call.
tour.p2desc: EV lost per 100 decisions is the thermometer. From about 200 decisions the direction is readable; comparing periods only becomes a claim once it survives the confidence interval.
tour.p3desc: ROI percentage is only representative from 30 tournaments with a known buy-in: below that a single cash distorts it, and the screen shows absolute profit instead.
tour.p4desc: Your mistakes grouped by spot and ranked by cost, not by frequency. This is what feeds the study plan and the drills, with nothing for you to choose.
tour.p5desc: The share of your decisions with a solver answer, and how closely you matched it. When a spot has no coverage the screen says so instead of inventing a verdict.
tour.p6desc: Every leak found turns into spaced-repetition drills. And validation does not happen in the drill: the platform goes back to your real hands to check whether you stopped leaking.

posProfile.title: Profile by position
posProfile.tooltip: How you play in EACH seat, on the five preflop decisions that have a chart: entering (VPIP), raising (PFR), opening (RFI), 3-betting and folding to a 3-bet after opening. The color compares with what the solver would do with your hands, in the seats, stacks and against the opponents you faced; each number's tooltip shows the band and the gap. The grid adds up all your hands, at any table size and any stack, so the reference is a range: the solver opens wider with fewer players left to act. For the close-up, with table size and stack fixed, click the RFI.
posProfile.legend: Green = within what the solver would do; red = outside (▲ more, ▼ less). Click RFI, 3-Bet or Fold 3-Bet to open the detail.
posProfile.inBand: Within the reference. Nothing to fix here.
posProfile.lowSampleLong: Not enough sample in this seat. The number exists, but it is not a reliable read yet.

vpip: you enter with fewer hands than the reference
you enter with more hands than the reference
pfr: you open less than the reference
you open more than the reference
fold_to_3bet: you fold to 3bet less than the reference
you fold to 3bet more than the reference
af: you play more passively than the reference
you play more aggressively than the reference
cbet_pct: you c-bet less than the reference
you c-bet more than the reference
steal_pct: you steal the blinds less than the reference
you steal the blinds more than the reference
wtsd: you go to showdown less than the reference
you go to showdown more than the reference
w_at_sd: you win fewer showdowns than the reference
you win more showdowns than the reference

posProfile.outsideGrid: Total includes {{n}} hands in positions outside the {{rows}} shown.
posProfile.descriptive: The grid describes your profile in each seat. The reference applies to the whole game, in the Total row.
posProfile.tableNote: Showing hands dealt to {{mesa}} players, the most frequent in your volume. Same seat, but with fewer players behind the solver opens wider.
posProfile.tableNoteAll: Adding up hands with any number of players. Pick a number to compare rows with each other: with fewer players behind, the same seat opens wider.
posProfile.lowSampleMatrix: Small sample: fewer than {{n}} opportunities. Your number is hidden; the solver reference is not, because it does not depend on the hands you were dealt.
posProfile.tableMix: This row comes from hands with: {{mix}}.
posProfile.rfiNaBB: The BB never opens: if everyone folds, the hand is over. So it has no RFI and no fold to 3-bet after opening.

rfi.above: You open {{delta}} points more than the solver from here.
rfi.below: You open {{delta}} points less than the solver from here.

threeBet.above: You 3-bet {{delta}} points more than the solver from here.
threeBet.below: You 3-bet {{delta}} points less than the solver from here.

fold3bet.above: You fold to 3-bets {{delta}} points more than the solver from here.
fold3bet.below: You fold to 3-bets {{delta}} points less than the solver from here.

generic.above: {{delta}} points above the solver from here.
generic.below: {{delta}} points below the solver from here.

vpip.above: You enter {{delta}} points more than the solver would with your hands.
vpip.below: You enter {{delta}} points less than the solver would with your hands.

pfr.above: You raise {{delta}} points more than the solver would with your hands.
pfr.below: You raise {{delta}} points less than the solver would with your hands.

detail.fold3bet: Fold to 3-bet after opening from {{pos}}, by who 3-bet
detail.note: Rows with fewer than {{n}} opportunities show the sample only. The solver band here varies only with stack, so it is narrower than the cell's.
detail.description: One row per opponent, with opportunities, your number and the solver band.

matrix.title: Hands opened from {{pos}}, against the solver
matrix.description: Two grids: the hands you opened from this seat and what the solver would open with the same hands and stacks; below, the largest divergences.
matrix.noDivergence: No hand with {{n}}+ occurrences sits {{pp}} points or more from the solver.
matrix.divergencesNote: Hands with {{n}} or more occurrences and {{pp}} points or more from the solver.
matrix.behind_one: At {{mesa}}-handed tables, only {{count}} player still acts after you. The fewer players left to act, the wider the solver opens.
matrix.behind_other: At {{mesa}}-handed tables, {{count}} players still act after you. The fewer players left to act, the wider the solver opens.
matrix.behindMixed: In this slice, the number of players still acting after you varies from hand to hand. The fewer players left to act, the wider the solver opens.
matrix.recorte: You in the {{pos}}, at {{mesa}}-handed tables, with {{stack}}. {{n}} times with an unopened pot.
matrix.bbNoRfi: The BB never opens the pot: when everyone folds, it takes the blinds without acting. So it has no RFI and no matrix.
matrix.sameHands: Both numbers are over the same {{n}} hands you were dealt in this slice.
matrix.sameHandsCovered: Both numbers are over the same {{n}} hands you were dealt in this slice, on the {{pct}}% that have a solver range.
matrix.smallSample: Small sample: fewer than {{n}} opportunities in this slice. The numbers are hidden; the grids and the divergence list are not.
matrix.noChartCompare: No solver range for this slice, so there is nothing to compare against.

posProfile.seatAbsent: Does not exist with {{mesa}} players dealt in. Whoever acted in that turn of the order is in the next seat.
